title: DIRTY-TREE does not affect overall or the exit code, so a run whose own summary says it is 'not valid as final acceptance evidence' still emits `overall: PASS` and exit 0 -- any CI or agent keying on the exit code cannot distinguish attributable from non-attributable evidence
evidence: scripts/live-verify.mjs:223-227 (overall is FAIL if any FAIL, else INCONCLUSIVE if any INCONCLUSIVE, else PASS -- DIRTY-TREE is in neither ladder) and :265 (`process.exit(overall === 'FAIL' ? 2 : overall === 'INCONCLUSIVE' ? 3 : 0)`). Both of my runs printed DIRTY-TREE at preflight and still ended `overall: PASS`, EXIT=0. NOTE: I explicitly tested the masking question the dispatch asked and DIRTY-TREE does NOT mask a real failure -- it is assigned at exactly one check (preflight attribution) and cannot suppress any other check's FAIL; that part of the design is sound.

Secondary, lower priority: each run's own evidence folder becomes an untracked entry that the NEXT run counts as a dirty file (I observed the count go 10 -> 11 between my two runs), so the tool slowly dirties the tree it measures unless evidence is committed after every run.

title: The fifth layer: `git ls-files --error-unmatch` proves only that the evidence PATH is tracked, never that its CONTENT matches the committed blob - so editing the already-committed preflight.json in place inflates the headline 20.2% -> 39.5% with --check AND pnpm lint:structure both exit 0 and NO uncommitted banner

title: The evidence content sha printed into docs/PROGRESS.md is line-ending dependent, so on a fresh clone (core.autocrlf=true, the default on Windows and set in this repo) --check reports STALE and lint:structure goes red with zero edits
evidence: Measured by checker: the committed blob for qa/evidence/live-2026-09-07-01-58-41/preflight.json is LF, 804 bytes (git cat-file -s 72f6690a = 804). After `git checkout -- <that path>` git materialises it as CRLF, 840 bytes, and the sha printed in the doc changes 5f7ed1c0d434 -> 3a73c60dcc6d, making docs/PROGRESS.md byte-different (sha256 1C028F7E... -> 5A8443C2...). With the evidence so materialised, 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'STALE: docs/PROGRESS.md differs from a fresh regeneration' exit 1, hence lint:structure red on an untouched clone. `git config core.autocrlf` = true in this repo. Regenerating 'fixes' it locally but produces a diff that flips straight back on an LF machine - a ping-pong diff between platforms. Note this compounds a PRE-EXISTING instance of the same class (git also warns that docs/PROGRESS.md itself is LF-in-worktree / CRLF-on-checkout, and generate() joins with \n), so I1 byte-for-byte re-derivability was already platform-dependent before this unit; this unit adds a second, independent CRLF-sensitive input.
fix_direction: Hash the LF-normalised content (raw.replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')) before printing the sha, or read the blob via `git show HEAD:<path>` so the sha is the committed bytes rather than the checkout's. Separately consider a .gitattributes entry pinning qa/evidence/**/*.json and docs/PROGRESS.md to `text eol=lf` so the whole class is closed.

title: A malformed or BOM-prefixed preflight.json is silently skipped, so the scorer can quietly fall back to stale evidence with no warning
evidence: Observed by checker while building an attack fixture: a preflight.json written with a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Out-File -Encoding utf8` produces) makes JSON.parse throw and is swallowed by `try { pre = JSON.parse(raw); } catch { continue; }` at scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:122. The run was silently ignored and the score was computed from the older evidence with no message at all. Fails SAFE here (it lowers rather than inflates, and the doc names whichever file it did use), which is why this is low and not high - but a newest legitimate run that is unreadable for any reason silently scores from stale data.
fix_direction: Strip a leading BOM before JSON.parse, and print a one-line warning naming any live-* candidate that could not be parsed instead of continuing in silence. Matches the sweep's silent-failure rule (a catch that swallows an error the caller needed).

A degraded re-index of an already-summarized session therefore replaces a real summary with a transcript slice, degrading that session's tree_index entry and /ask answers until someone re-indexes. Confirmed live 2026-09-07 as a side effect of the ISS-056 proof: the degraded run wrote its labelled fallback page and still flipped status.index to done.
fix_direction: Same shape as the accepted ISS-056 fix: give summarizeSession a discriminated result and, when degraded, keep an existing session_pages doc instead of replacing it - writing the labelled fallback only when the session has no page yet. Contract criterion 1a (added this cycle) now authorizes exactly this; criterion 1 still requires the fallback to exist for a first index.
checker_verdict: RAISED BY THE MAKER, which disclosed it and deliberately did not act because 'the contract explicitly requires that fallback'. Ruled by /checker Mode A cycle 1: the maker was RIGHT on both counts - right that it is the same bug wearing a label, and right not to rewrite checker-owned ground truth in order to fix it. The contract required the fallback to EXIST, never to REPLACE a good page; that ambiguity is now removed by criterion 1a. Filed MEDIUM rather than high, and explicitly NOT a failure of the claims-degradation-honesty unit: unlike the claims defect it is clearly labelled rather than silent, destroys no human-curated review state, and is fully regenerable from the retained turns. | Mode A re-check 2026-09-07 (unit summarize-degradation-honesty, cycle 1): PASS. Fix verified by mutation (disabled the existingPage lookup; reddened exactly the 2 claimed tests, all others green), by both write-direction tests, and by independent reproduction of the disclosed live-Mongo timeout (2/2 checker-authored attempts also timed out). Status -> fixed (verified pending a future live end-to-end proof once Mongo recovers).

title: Nothing pins the tenantId in indexSession's raw claims/session_pages/tree_index queries - stripping it survives the entire suite AND typecheck, and destroys other tenants' claims
evidence: CHECKER MUTATION, unlisted by the manifest, added by /checker Mode A cycle 1: removing tenantId from apps/api/src/indexing.ts:94 - deleteMany({ tenantId, 'evidence.sessionId': sessionId }) becomes deleteMany({ 'evidence.sessionId': sessionId }), occurrence count 1 -> 0 asserted before running - leaves apps/api 69/69 GREEN and tsc --noEmit -p apps/api/tsconfig.json exit 0. It is not a harmless mutation: run live against the real database with two scratch tenants sharing a sessionId, the mutated delete took BOTH from 1 -> 0, destroying an unrelated tenant's claims. The escape hatch is that claims, session_pages and tree_index are reached through the RAW db.collection(name) rather than through scopedCollection, whose whole purpose (packages/db/src/lib/tenantScope.ts:26-42) is to make a tenant-less query a compile error; those three carry their tenantId by hand in the filter instead.
fix_direction: Cheap now, and it was not before: this unit ADDED the db injection that makes it testable. Upgrade the fake in apps/api/src/indexing.test.ts to record the FILTER as well as the op name (it currently records only {coll, op}) and assert every claims/session_pages/tree_index filter carries its tenantId. Structurally better: extend scopedCollection with deleteMany/insertMany/replaceOne so these three stop needing the raw handle at all.
checker_verdict: NOT a defect introduced by this unit and NOT a verdict failure - the pre-fix code at HEAD reached the same three collections through getDb().collection(...) with the same hand-written tenantId, so the injected-db refactor did not weaken tenant scoping. Verified positively too: scopedCollection still builds all three of its accessors (turns/sessions/session_pages) from the injected handle, every raw filter still carries its tenantId, and the live run confirmed a second tenant's claim survived BOTH a degraded and a healthy re-index. Filed because it is a safety-critical invariant with nothing pinning it - the fifth instance of this project's recurring untested-guard pattern (ISS-030, ISS-038, ISS-048, ISS-056), and the manifest itself argues the lesson should be applied at the cause rather than disclosed again.
checker_note: FIXED, verified by /checker Mode A cycle 1 on evidence I produced myself. The fix is at the cause: scopedCollection gained deleteMany/insertMany (tenant-merged via withTenant), and claims + session_pages now route through it instead of the raw handle. Re-ran the original mutation with occurrence count asserted 1->0: apps/api goes 70/71 RED (it was GREEN before this unit). Live, with my OWN script (not the maker's) against the real db lkb, two scratch tenants chk060-A/B sharing one unique sessionId: fixed code HEALTHY A=1 B=1, DEGRADED A=1 B=1, B's human-'verified' claim intact=true; same script with the mutation applied HEALTHY A=1 B=0, intact=false. Cleanup read back from the server A=0 B=0 on every run.

title: tree_index has no tenantId field at all - a tenant's whole knowledge tree is separated only by a tenant:<id> string prefix inside node_id, which scopedCollection cannot reach and the compiler cannot enforce
evidence: Confirmed by reading schema/tree_index.schema.json: properties are node_id/title/level/summary/evidence/children - no tenantId, so TreeIndexNode does not satisfy scopedCollection's 'T extends {tenantId: string}' and a {tenantId} filter would match zero rows. CHECKER RULING: the maker was RIGHT to refuse a schema migration inside a bug-fix unit, and the prefix convention is ACCEPTABLE AS AN INTERIM boundary - node_id functions as a primary key, tenant separation by prefixed primary key is a legitimate pattern, tree_index takes no destructive multi-document op (only findOne plus a single-document replaceOne upsert), and both call sites in indexing.ts now share one treeIndexRootFilter() and are pinned by indexing.test.ts. It is NOT acceptable as a permanent end state: it leaves two classes of collection with different enforcement properties, which is precisely the asymmetry that produced ISS-060. title: createMongoHealthDeps().checkHealth() only catches the ping failure; a countDocuments() throw (post-ping) is unhandled and apps/api has no error-handling middleware/asyncHandler wrapper, so the health route's own documented promise ("REPORT an unhealthy backend, never crash reporting it") does not hold for this path
evidence: apps/api/src/store.ts createMongoHealthDeps() (~line 250-269): try/catch wraps only `await db.command({ping:1})`; the subsequent `Promise.all(names.map(name => db.collection(name).countDocuments()))` and the `readFileSync(SCHEMA_INDEX_PATH)` call sit outside any try/catch. apps/api/src/routes/health.ts's handler does `const report = await deps.checkHealth();` with no try/catch of its own. Repo-wide grep across apps/api/src for an error-handling middleware/asyncHandler pattern (`app.use((err`, `.catch(next)`, `asyncHandler`) found zero matches -- this is not health-route-specific, it is the repo's existing pattern (most routes, including the same-range citations.ts/graph.ts, also have no per-call try/catch), but health.ts's own file comment specifically claims the opposite ("the route's whole job is to REPORT an unhealthy backend, never crash reporting it") for a path that only covers the ping. A single flaky countDocuments call (e.g. a transient network blip between the ping succeeding and the count starting) becomes an unhandled promise rejection on the liveness probe itself -- the one route ops depends on being reliably answerable.
fix_direction: wrap the Promise.all(...)/readFileSync block in its own try/catch inside checkHealth() and fall back to {db:"error", collections:{}} (or a partial-count shape) on failure, matching the ping branch's own contract; alternatively wrap health.ts's route handler in a try/catch that maps any throw to a 503, so the liveness probe itself never 500s/hangs on a transient store error
fixed_evidence: Extracted apps/api/src/health-probe.ts's probeMongoHealth(ping, countAll), wrapping both steps in one try/catch, degrading to {db:"error", collections:{}} on any failure; store.ts's createMongoHealthDeps() now delegates to it. 3 new tests in health-probe.test.ts (happy path, ping failure, and the ISS-070 regression: countAll failure after a successful ping). Checker independently reproduced the mutation test (reverted to the exact buggy two-try/catch shape, confirmed via diff, re-ran: 2/3 pass with the regression test reddening on an unhandled-rejection-style AssertionError, restored, 3/3 and 5/5 green again) and a live check against real Mongo (happy path db:ok with 21 real collection counts; probeMongoHealth with a throwing countAll returns {db:"error",collections:{}} rather than rejecting). pnpm --filter @lkb/api typecheck, pnpm -r typecheck, pnpm --filter @lkb/api test (85/85), pnpm lint:structure, and node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs (21.9%/30.7%, 57 features, unchanged) all clean. verdict qa/verdicts/health-route-error-hardening.md, checker PASS cycle 1.

title: data/eval/golden-set.json saturates recall@5 at 1.000 with zero misses, so plan §10 U0.10's prescribed remedy ("redo T-021/T-022 against a real LLM") cannot produce a falsifiable retrieval number, and U1.4/U1.5's recall gates are unfailable against the same set
evidence: Measured by this checker, not taken from the manifest. Own run of node scripts/eval-recall.mjs: recall@5 = 1.000 (46/46 hits, misses: []), question-blind control = 0.217, VERDICT: SATURATED. Chance floor re-derived independently from the raw data rather than from assessBaseline: the deterministic blind top-5 of the 23 real session ids covers 10 of the 46 questions = 0.2174, exactly 5/23 -- the control lands ON the floor and does not exceed it, so the control is not leaking question signal and 0.217 is a true floor. Lift = +0.783: the heuristic retriever beats chance decisively, so this is NOT a claim that the retriever is bad. The defect is in the instrument's headroom. Provenance re-derived: scripts/gen-golden-set.mjs (header, lines 3-6) builds the questions from session_page.keyInsights as verbatim excerpts, and 0 of 46 questions end with a question mark -- all 46 are declarative machine-generated statements (e.g. "New Zealand: 76% of 2025 visa applications approved, government target is 27,000 Indian students by 2030."), drawn from the same pipeline and the same document as the retrieval target that heuristic-retriever.ts scores against. Consequence, from the plan text itself (C:/Users/Lenovo/.claude/plans/thik-hai-and-you-nested-cat.md:1251-1254, :1281-1282, :1287-1288): a metric already pinned at its maximum can register a regression but can never demonstrate an improvement, so U0.10 would spend real LLM budget to produce a second unfalsifiable number; U1.4 requires "recall@5 reported as a delta against the U0.10 baseline" (a delta that can only be <= 0); and U1.5's "recall@5 >= 0.85" target is cleared by anything not actively broken. Two weaker framings of this finding were checked and are NOT the defect: (a) verbatim-substring tautology is FALSE -- 0 of 74 keyInsights across all 23 pages appear verbatim in their own page summary, so an exact-substring matcher would score 0.000, not 1.000; (b) "the retriever is worthless" is FALSE -- see the +0.783 lift. The real mechanism is same-source vocabulary leakage plus ceiling saturation.
scoping_note: Scoped narrower than the manifest asserted. U0.10 has three halves and only one is saturated: (i) the recall@5 half IS saturated and cannot produce a falsifiable number on this set; (ii) the judge-agreement half (T-022 evaluator calibration) is a DIFFERENT instrument and is not shown saturated by this evidence -- it is not blocked by this issue; (iii) "file the retraction of the heuristic-proxy PASS" is worth doing unconditionally and depends on no question set at all. The manifest's blanket phrasing ("U0.10 as written cannot produce a falsifiable number") is correct on (i) and overbroad on (ii)/(iii). Severity is unchanged by that correction. Conversely the manifest UNDER-scoped the blast radius: the same saturation disarms U1.4's delta gate and U1.5's >= 0.85 gate, not just U0.10.
fix_direction: Do NOT schedule U0.10 against the current set. Prerequisite is golden-set-redesign, which is a HUMAN_GATE (question authorship is a judgment call, and the plan's own T-022 design requires two human graders): questions written from the TRANSCRIPTS rather than from the summaries being retrieved (kills the shared-vocabulary leak), phrased as actual user questions rather than declarative statements, deliberately including near-neighbour sessions so some answers are contestable, and every recall figure thereafter reported next to its question-blind control per qa/contracts/eval-baseline-control.md [I1]. Also amend T-021's done_check: recall@5 >= 0.85 against a set that returns 1.000 by construction is not a criterion. NOTE: that human gate is ALREADY OPEN -- the maker's 2026-09-08T01:35 tick escalated exactly this to the user and stopped, and the 2026-09-08 Mode B sweep (qa/QUEUE.md item 1) confirmed it. No new GRILL row is raised by this issue; re-asking a question already sitting with the human is the D-006 anti-pattern.
reconciliation: The 2026-09-08 Mode B sweep independently reached the same conclusion (qa/QUEUE.md, "The golden-set question -- independent assessment") at the same severity (high) and deliberately did NOT file, deferring the ledger row to this unit's checker to avoid two rows for one defect. This is that row. Not a duplicate -- the reconciliation the sweep asked for. The sweep's one stale handoff (baseline.ts:63 hardcoded "saturated = false", observed on untracked in-flight code) was fixed before submission and is verified computed at baseline.ts:63 as of this check.
fixed_evidence: Resolved by unit golden-set-regeneration (qa/verdicts/golden-set-regeneration.md, PASS cycle 2). The saturation this issue names is gone: recall@5 1.000 -> 0.307 (23/75) with 52 misses and a 0.187 question-blind control, and assessBaseline's verdict moved saturated -> informative. Gate condition 2 satisfied (strictly inside the 0.217-1.000 band with non-zero misses), so no Option B escalation. title: createMongoSearchDeps' token derivation is unpinned by any test: reintroducing the exact `length > 2` defect this unit exists to prevent -- in search-store.ts, the file that actually ships it -- leaves typecheck and all 148 tests green
evidence: CHECKER MUTATION, independent of the manifest. Edited apps/api/src/search-store.ts:48 from `const tokens = lexicalQueryTokens(query);` to `const tokens = lexicalQueryTokens(query).filter((t) => t.length > 2);`, confirmed the change via diff against a backup, then ran: `pnpm -r typecheck` exit 0 (all 10 projects Done), `pnpm --filter @lkb/api test` 89/89 PASS, `pnpm --filter @lkb/index test` 59/59 PASS. Root cause: apps/api/src has no test that exercises createMongoSearchDeps at all -- search.test.ts drives the route through fakeSearchDeps() (apps/api/src/fixtures.ts), never the Mongo deps, and there is no search-store.test.ts. lexical.test.ts's PROPERTY test proves the superset property OF lexicalQueryTokens, but nothing asserts that the store CONSUMES it unfiltered -- the property is proven about a function the shipped code is free to stop using correctly. title: The pre-filter's superset guarantee has a narrow Unicode case-folding hole: a turn whose text contains U+0130 or U+212A can be scored by the JS tokenizer but missed by Mongo's $options:'i' regex
evidence: CHECKER ANALYSIS + live corpus probe, not disclosed by the manifest. The superset argument is sound for ASCII and holds for accented text, but it silently assumes JS `String.toLowerCase()` and Mongo's ASCII-only `$options: "i"` agree. They do not for the handful of characters whose lowercase mapping crosses into ASCII. Concretely: `'İ'.toLowerCase()` in JS is `'i' + U+0307`, so a turn containing `İnvestment` tokenizes (packages/index/src/search/lexical.ts:24, split on /\W+/, U+0307 being \W) to the tokens ['i','nvestment'] -- the scorer would score it for query token 'i' -- while Mongo's /i/i against the raw stored text matches neither 'i' nor 'I' and the turn is never fetched. U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowercases to 'k' with the same effect. Note the reverse direction is safe: because tokenize() splits on JS non-unicode \W, every token is [A-Za-z0-9_] only, so accented input (cafe-with-acute, Devanagari, CJK) never produces a non-ASCII token -- checker verified live that the query "cafe-with-acute" and "İnvestment" both returned byte-identical results on the new and old paths. LIVE IMPACT TODAY: ZERO. Read-only probe of the real `toc` tenant (2118 turns): countDocuments({text:{$regex:'İ'}}) = 0 and countDocuments({text:{$regex:'K'}}) = 0 (51 turns do carry other non-ASCII characters, none of them hazardous). Filed so the property is recorded rather than rediscovered, and because the contract now states the superset guarantee as an invariant (I6) which should carry its own stated bound.
fix_direction: No code change warranted today (zero corpus occurrences, and the fix -- normalizing text at ingest, or adding a $expr/collation-aware filter -- costs more than the hazard). Recorded as a bounded exception on contract invariant I6. Revisit only if the corpus starts carrying Turkish/Azeri text or Unicode symbol characters; the cheap mitigation would be NFKC-normalizing `text` at ingest so the stored form and the tokenizer agree.

title: search-prefilter.ts's own docstring contradicts the unit's escapeRegex finding: it presents escaping as live correctness/DoS protection for a path the tokenizer makes unreachable

title: Post-fetch resolution is unasserted -- misresolving every hit's turn or session, or dropping session deduplication, all leave 102/102 green; the fake's id-blind findOne is why
evidence: THREE CHECKER-ORIGINAL MUTATIONS (bypasses 5C, 5D, 5F) during the search-store-injectable-handle cycle-1 check, all in apps/api/src/search-store.ts, each diff-confirmed against a byte-backup and restored byte-identically. (5C) `session: sessionById.get(hit.sessionId) ?? null` -> `session: sessions[0] ?? null` -- every hit carries the FIRST session regardless of which session it came from: 102/102 green. (5D) `turn: turnById.get(hit.turnId) ?? null` -> `turn: turns[0] ?? null` -- every hit carries the first turn's text: 102/102 green. (5F) `const sessionIds = [...new Set(scored.map((s) => s.sessionId))]` -> `scored.map((s) => s.sessionId)` -- the Set is gone, so a findOne is issued per HIT rather than per DISTINCT session: 102/102 green. That last one is a direct break of contract [C10] ('Session lookups are deduplicated ... one findOne per distinct session id, not per hit') and of [I3] ('a future edit reintroducing a per-hit findOne is a contract break'), and it is invisible to the entire suite. ROOT CAUSE, and the reason this is filed as one row: capturingDb()'s fake (search-store.test.ts:34-46) returns the SAME SESSION object for every findOne regardless of _id, and returns the whole CORPUS from find() regardless of filter, so id-keyed resolution cannot be falsified by it; and the only end-to-end test (line 96, query 'visa') returns exactly ONE hit, which is precisely the case where a broken Map lookup and a correct one agree. 5C and 5D are answer-CORRUPTION rather than answer-loss: the caller receives a plausible-looking hit whose transcript text and session title belong to a different conversation, which is worse than a missing hit because nothing about it looks wrong. WHAT THE TEST DOES CATCH, recorded so it gets due credit: a fourth checker mutation returning each hit twice (`[...scored, ...scored].map(...)`) DID redden test 3 at 101/102, so the end-to-end test is not inert -- it is just too small a sample. NOT A LIVE DEFECT: the shipped resolution is correct, and live read-only parity against production Mongo was IDENTICAL on turnIds and scores across 8 queries. Disclosed in advance by the manifest's checklist item 4 ('the turn/session resolution after the fetch ... downstream of everything this unit pins'), which is why it is filed at medium and did not block the PASS.
fix_direction: Make the fake honour ids and make the end-to-end case bigger -- both small changes to apps/api/src/search-store.test.ts. (1) capturingDb()'s findOne should look the requested _id up in a small SESSIONS map and return null for a miss, and should record every findOne filter it receives. That alone kills 5C. (2) Add one end-to-end assertion over a query matching turns in TWO different sessions with different titles, checking each hit's turn.text and session.title match its own turnId/sessionId -- that kills 5C and 5D together. (3) Assert the recorded sessions-findOne count equals the number of DISTINCT sessionIds among the hits, not the hit count -- that is [C10]/[I3] made machine-checkable for the first time, and it is the cheapest of the three.

title: search-store.ts's comment justifies per-call db resolution with a claim inverted relative to the only entrypoint: index.ts awaits connect() BEFORE buildProductionDeps()
evidence: CHECKER VERIFICATION of a rationale the manifest asserted twice (in the manifest body and in the shipped comment) and that this checker checked rather than accepted. apps/api/src/search-store.ts:56-57 reads 'Resolved per call, not at construction: production builds these deps at boot, before connect().' title: gemini and ollama embed() accept a response whose vector COUNT is correct but whose vectors are all EMPTY - returns {dims: 0} instead of throwing, because both guards are relative (count vs count, length vs length[0]) and neither has a floor

Cause: the count check compares vectors.length to texts.length (3===3, passes) and the ragged check computes dims = vectors[0]?.length ?? 0 = 0, then finds no vector differing from 0, so findIndex returns -1 and the function returns. title: buildChunks emits DUPLICATE chunks - a chunk whose turnRefs are byte-identical to its predecessor - whenever the carried-over overlap turn alone would exceed maxChars; the manifest claim 'no chunk duplicates its predecessor' is false on a TWO-TURN input
evidence: CHECKER-UNIT chunk-schema-and-chunker cycle 1, my own property fuzz (scratchpad/fuzz-chunks.ts, 3024 shapes: 24 hand-built awkward sequences + 3000 randomized). Identical-to-predecessor chunks in 1172/3024 shapes; fully-subsumed-by-predecessor in 11015 chunk pairs. MINIMAL REPRO, default options: buildChunks with two turns of 700 and 500 chars returns [{0,[t0]},{1,[t0]},{2,[t0,t1]}] - chunks 0 and 1 are the same 700 chars with the same single turnRef. Turn lengths [900,900,900] give the same shape. [5,5,5000,5,5] emits chunk2=[t2], wholly contained in both its neighbours. ROOT CAUSE at packages/index/src/chunk/build-chunks.ts:86 - after flush() carries the tail forward (:78), `current` holds ONLY already-emitted turns, so when the next turn trips the `chars + len > maxChars` guard, flush() re-emits that carried tail as a standalone chunk. The guard's `current.length > 0` test cannot distinguish a real in-progress chunk from a pure overlap carry. NOT silent turn loss: coverage, never-split, ordering, blank-exclusion and tail-retention all HELD across all 3024 shapes with 0 violations each.
fix_direction: At build-chunks.ts:86, flush only when `current` holds at least one turn not already emitted - the same un-emitted test the tail block at :93-94 already performs; hoist it into a helper (hasNewTurns(current)) used in both places so the two cannot drift. Alternative: drop the overlap carry instead of flushing it when the incoming turn cannot fit. Add a regression assertion over generated shapes rather than one fixture: no two chunks share an identical turnRefs list, and no chunk's turnRefs are a subset of its predecessor's.

title: buildChunks' documented HARD CEILING maxChars is not a ceiling - 37% of multi-turn chunks exceed it, up to 2.2x - because the overlap carry is re-added after the guard has already run
evidence: CHECKER-UNIT chunk-schema-and-chunker cycle 1, measured (scratchpad/max.ts): over 4000 random sessions of 1-20 turns of 0-900 chars, 22885 of 61352 multi-turn chunks exceeded maxChars=800; worst observed 1790 chars for a 2-turn chunk. The single-over-long-turn exemption is deliberate, documented, and EXCLUDED from this count - these are multi-turn chunks only. build-chunks.ts:44 states 'Hard ceiling: a chunk never starts a new turn that would carry it past this'; plan section 10 U1.2 specifies '~400-800 chars'. Minimal repro, default options: turns of 700 and 500 chars yield a final chunk of 1201 chars. Same root cause as ISS-098 - flush() at :78 restores the overlap tail into `current` and resets `chars` to its length, so the :86 guard is evaluated against a chunk that then grows by the overlap PLUS the new turn.
fix_direction: Fix with ISS-098 - one change closes both. After deciding to flush, the next chunk starts from the overlap and the incoming turn should be admitted only if overlapChars + len <= maxChars; when it is not, start the chunk WITHOUT the overlap rather than emitting the overlap alone. Then assert the ceiling over generated shapes: every chunk with turnRefs.length > 1 has text.length <= maxChars. If the ceiling is genuinely meant to be soft in the presence of overlap, the doc comment at :44 and the plan's '~400-800' must say so - but silently is not an option.
blocks: Chunk width drives embedding cost and retrieval precision: a 2.2x breach means U1.4's recall@5 is measured over chunks materially wider than the design the plan specifies, and a provider token limit sized against 800 chars can be exceeded with no code path noticing.
fix_evidence: CHECKER-UNIT chunk-schema-and-chunker cycle 2. Measured against the emitted string, never an internal counter: over 3192 generated shapes / 9079 MULTI-TURN chunks, ZERO exceed maxChars (cycle 1: 22885/61352, 37%, worst 1790 vs 800). The single-over-long-turn exemption is excluded from the count, as in cycle 1. Six option sets exercised including targetChars===maxChars and the perverse {targetChars:900,maxChars:800}. A THIRD, related bug the maker found with its own fuzz is closed with it: measure() summed trimmed turn lengths while the emitted text joins turns with a space, so the ceiling was off by (n-1) - an 802-char chunk against an 800 ceiling. measure() at build-chunks.ts:53-55 now adds Math.max(0, turns.length-1) and :101 adds the separator to len; my P3b asserts chunk.text.length === sum(trimmed)+(n-1) AND the byte-exact join form, 0 violations / 22872 chunks. TRADEOFF JUDGED AND QUANTIFIED (scratchpad/seams.ts, scratchpad/nec.ts): when carried overlap plus the next turn cannot fit, the overlap is now dropped rather than the ceiling breached. Accepted as the correct trade.

Differential run of the same 23 probes at HEAD and at d367253 (the gate reverted, everything else identical) - these SHIPPED before the gate and REFUSE after it: "Ruby speaking here." | "Ruby speaking and I lead admissions." | "Ruby speaking today from Pune." | "Ruby speaking again." | "Ruby speaking now." | "Ruby speaking -- good to be here." | "Ruby speaking as the panel chair." | "Ruby speaking (admissions)." | "Ruby speaking\u2026 thanks all." | "Ruby speaking over Zoom." Every one is the self-identification idiom the `speaking` cue exists to admit, and "Ruby" is verbatim in the turn. Root cause, packages/index/src/pipeline/speaker-name-rules.ts:205-208: SPEAKING_NAMES admits only end-of-string, one of [.,!?;:], or one of nine prepositions (from|on|at|for|with|to|in|of|about); everything else falls to `if (SPEAKING_ANY.test(rawAfter)) return false;` which is an UNCONDITIONAL early return that also short-circuits every downstream cue branch. So a following adverb (here/again/now/today), a conjunction (and), a dash, a parenthesis, a Unicode ellipsis, or a preposition outside the nine (as, over, after, before, during, via) all refuse. ISS-097's own recorded fix_direction listed `today` and `now` in the permitted set; the implementation dropped both. The suite cannot see any of this: reverting the whole gate reddens exactly ONE test, so there is zero standing coverage on the recall side of the gate. Not caused by this gate and NOT charged: "\u0930\u0942\u092c\u0940 speaking." refuses at both HEAD and baseline (pre-existing shape guard, gap 4's English-only note).
fix_direction: [C1]/[C13]. Two separable defects. (1) Make the refusal LOCAL, not an early return: the `speaking` branch should decline to supply a cue and fall through to the remaining branches rather than `return false` for the whole predicate. (2) Replace the closed preposition allowlist with the actual discriminator, which is the one the manifest itself states: refuse only when `speaking` is followed by a NOUN it modifies (i.e. a following bare noun-phrase head that continues the clause). Everything else - end of clause, punctuation, dash, parenthesis, ellipsis, conjunction, adverb, or ANY preposition - is the idiom and must keep resolving. Then pin the recall side: the mutation that reverts the gate must redden a recall test as well as the English refusal test, or the gate is only half-measured. Measure recall against a recorded set, not a self-chosen one - the "all 14 probes correct" claim in this manifest is the same self-selected-denominator habit D-015 exists to stop, this time on the recall side instead of the refusal side. Separately and LOW, not blocking: the manifest states "the duplicated comment block from the earlier edit is gone"; it is still present at speaker-name-rules.ts:193-203, two paraphrases of the same paragraph.

title: The C8 write-time correlation assertions throw OUTSIDE indexSession's try/catch, so a malformed embedder result skips chunks correctly but also skips tree_index and the status.index flip - leaving the session permanently `pending`
evidence: CHECKER PROBE against 11a90b0, real indexSession imported from a temporary probe file since removed (tree verified clean). 12-turn fixture -> 12 real chunks, fake db recording every collection op. embed throws (P1) / rejects (P2) / returns undefined (P3): chunkOps=[] AND claims+tree_index+sessions.updateOne all run, no throw - correct. embed returns {dims:3} with no vectors key (P4): TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)'; 2 vectors for 1 chunk (P5); 1 vector for 12 chunks (P6); dims:99 vs 2-long vectors (P7); an empty vector at index 1 (P8); ragged 5-long at index 1 with dims 3 (P9) - in ALL SIX the assertion propagates out of indexSession, tree_index NEVER runs and sessions.updateOne({'status.index':'done'}) NEVER runs. chunkOps=[] in all nine, so no data is destroyed - this is an availability/consistency defect, not the ISS-056 shape. Cause, apps/api/src/indexing.ts:156-163: the try/catch wraps ONLY `await deps.embed(...)`; the count assertion (:169) and the per-chunk dims assertion (:176) sit after it, as does the doc-building loop. The caller (ingest-store.ts/whatsapp-store.ts, contract C4) logs and swallows the rejection, and nothing in the system re-triggers indexing, so the session stays status.index:'pending' and absent from the Brain tree forever. This is exactly the trade the code comment at :157-158 and the manifest both say they refuse ('failing the whole call would turn no-vectors-this-run into no summary, no claims, no tree'). NOT LIVE-REACHABLE TODAY, which is why this is medium and not high: packages/ai/src/providers/gemini.ts:117-139 and ollama.ts:98-118 each already refuse a wrong count, an all-empty set and a ragged set, throwing INSIDE deps.embed where the catch handles them (that is P1/P2, which pass cleanly). config/ai-routing.yaml:16 declares embedding:[gemini,ollama], so both configured paths are guarded; the gap opens when a third provider is added or a router path returns a result the providers did not construct.

Move the two assertions (and the chunkDocs build) inside the SAME try, or wrap the whole `if (embedded)` block, so an inconsistent batch degrades to 'chunks left unchanged' with a warning - identical to every other embed failure - instead of aborting indexSession. The refusals themselves are correct and must NOT be weakened: nothing inconsistent may reach insertMany. Then pin it: a test asserting that a malformed embed result still leaves claims written, tree_index updated and status.index flipped to 'done'. The two existing assert.rejects tests pin the throw but read the collateral as acceptable.

Re-derived by a checker-authored 12-turn probe (3 chunks) across all nine attack shapes - chunks saw ZERO ops AND tree_index.replaceOne ran AND sessions.updateOne({'status.index':'done'}) ran, in all nine. Regression guard confirmed real by mutation: mutate.mjs apply apps/api/src/indexing.ts, catch re-narrowed so assertion errors escape (the ISS-112 shape) -> the two rewritten indexing.test.ts tests FAIL (17 tests, 15 pass, 2 fail) and 5 of my own probes redden; restored via mutate.mjs restore, assert-clean OK. title: The three LARGEST sessions silently produce zero chunks: one unbatched embed() call fails on them and indexing.ts discards the skip result
evidence: Measured live by the sweep against lkb, read-only. The sessions with NO chunks are exactly the top 3 by turn count: 2026-04-21-visa-blueprint-part2-italy-france-nz (291 turns), 2026-07-15-creative-futures (269), 2026-08-10-ucas-what-changed-what-matters (230). The largest session that DID chunk has 134 turns. The cutoff is monotone between 230 and 134 -- size-dependent, not content-dependent. 790 of 2118 turns (37% of the corpus) are absent from the vector index; 1328 are covered, and 2118-1328=790 exactly. Cause: apps/api/src/indexing.ts:100 embeds every plan in ONE call, embed({ texts: plans.map((p) => p.text) }), with no batching and no size bound; the catch at indexing.ts:134-141 returns { written: 0, skipped: 'embedding-failed' } after a console.warn; and indexing.ts:224-225 DISCARDS that return value, so indexSession reports success and no job row, session field or ledger records the loss. Consequence: /search over the vector layer is silently blind to the three biggest transcripts and every downstream recall number is computed over 63% of the corpus while presenting as complete. This is the first live exercise of the U1.3 write path -- no prior PASS on this seam was measured against real rows.

title: The vector-pending gap _id is not tenant-namespaced, so a sessionId shared by two tenants makes recordVectorGap throw E11000 and abort the rest of indexSession
evidence: Checker-authored LIVE run against real Mongo (lkb, scratch tenants chk118-a/chk118-b, 2026-09-08). recordVectorGap derives `_id = `vector-pending:${sessionId}`` (apps/api/src/indexing/vector-gap.ts:39), which is globally unique in `gaps` while the filter is tenant-merged. Tenant B upserting a gap for a sessionId tenant A already has: `E11000 duplicate key error collection: lkb.gaps index: _id_ dup key: { _id: "vector-pending:chk118-sess-1" }`. Tenant ISOLATION HOLDS - A's row stayed owned by A, B created no row, and the collection carried zero tenant-less rows - so this is availability, not disclosure. Reachable, not theoretical: whatsapp-store.ts:132 sets `sessionId = source._id`, a sha256 of (groupJid, ownerUserId) with no tenantId in it, so two tenants tracking the same group produce the same sessionId. Consequence: the throw escapes recordVectorGap, and session.ts:237 places that call BEFORE the tree_index update and the `status.index` flip, so the session is left `"pending"` forever while the ingest still returns 201 (criterion 4 swallows the indexing rejection).
fix_direction: Namespace the derived id by tenant (`vector-pending:<tenantId>:<sessionId>`), or make recordVectorGap non-fatal to indexSession by moving the call after the tree_index/status steps or wrapping it. Prefer the id change: it is one line and keeps the failure surface intact. Note the same collision class already exists for `sessions`/`sources` upserts in whatsapp-store.ts:142 and predates this unit - out of scope here, worth a separate look.

title: The claims tagging write is asserted on its BODY but not on its TARGETING: both the find scope and the updateOne filter can be widened to {} with apps/api still 139/139 green
evidence: Checker, promote-tree-entities cycle 3, derived by mutation at f3ded7c (unit files untouched since 5310c25). Cycle 3 correctly closed ISS-126 item (4) - I re-derived it: `{ $set: { topicRefs: refs } }` -> `{ $set: { topicRefs: [] } }` now gives 138 pass / 1 fail, killed by `ISS-126(4): tagClaims writes the session's REAL topicRefs onto each of its claims`. But the NEXT layer of the same seam survives. Two further mutations on apps/api/src/indexing/promote-entities.ts, each applied via mutate.mjs, tested, restored, assert-clean: (a) line 97 `.find({ "evidence.sessionId": sessionId })` -> `.find({})` => 139 pass / 0 fail, SURVIVES; (b) line 99 `.updateOne({ _id: c._id }, ...)` -> `.updateOne({}, ...)` => 139 pass / 0 fail, SURVIVES. Cause: the 9 writer tests assert what the update BODY contains (topicRefs value, tenantId, upsert options) and how MANY calls occur, but never assert the filters recorded in `calls[].filter` - even though fakeDb DOES record them, so the assertion is cheap. fakeDb.find also ignores its filter and returns opts.claims unconditionally, which is why (a) is invisible; the second cycle-3 test even seeds a claim whose evidence.sessionId is "other" and still expects it visited, so the fixture actively cannot distinguish scoped from unscoped. Downstream consequence: this runs LIVE inside indexSession on every ingest. With the find scope widened, indexing one session would overwrite topicRefs on EVERY claim in the tenant (81 today) with that session's topics - last-session-wins silent corpus-wide corruption, invisible to the suite. Tenancy itself is NOT at risk (scopedCollection confines by tenant and test 4 covers the body), so this is data-integrity within a tenant, not a cross-tenant leak. The shipped filters are CORRECT as written; this is an undefended-targeting coverage gap, the third instance on this seam of 'the mutation is invisible because the fixture cannot reach the branch'.
fix_direction: Two assertions on the already-recorded calls, in apps/api/src/indexing/promote-entities.test.ts: (1) assert the claims `find` call's filter deep-equals { "evidence.sessionId": sessionId }; (2) assert each claims `updateOne` filter deep-equals { _id: <that claim's _id> }, matched pairwise against the seeded fixture. Additionally make fakeDb.find on `claims` actually FILTER opts.claims by evidence.sessionId rather than returning all of them - otherwise a scoping regression stays undetectable no matter what is asserted, and fix the cycle-3 test that seeds sessionId "other" and expects it visited, which encodes the wrong behaviour as expected. PRECONDITION: this must be closed BEFORE U2.2/U2.3 turns on any live entity backfill - today topics=0/orgs=0 and all 81 claims are untagged, so nothing is corrupted yet, but the first real ingest runs this path for real. Non-numeric id deliberately: the max(existing)+1 counter is held by a concurrent lane (qa/gates/ledger-id-collision.md), same precedent as ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-005.

title: verdictCycle() counts prose in four unfenced shapes -- the UNSAFE direction against the module's own documented 'undercounting is safe' claim

Cycle checked: 9

title: The phase-3 scorer's citation-validity test is circular: it re-asks the SAME production rule that accepted the identity, so bar-2's 'zero wrong citation links' half is structurally non-falsifiable and reports invalidCount:0 while a spk:3 identity is evidenced solely by a spk:1 turn
evidence: qa/evidence/u2-4-phase3-precision-regate-2026-09-22/05-score.mjs:258-274. The ISS-255 case-4 check imports packages/index/src/pipeline/speaker-name-rules.ts and validates each accepted evidence pair with `rules.containsNameVerbatim(t.text, displayName)` && `rules.citesNameAsAnIntroduction(t.text, displayName)` -- the identical predicate extractSpeakers used to ACCEPT that identity. Any identity the pipeline accepted via that cue rule therefore passes the citation test by construction. It never checks that the cited turn belongs to (or is spoken by) the label being identified. Measured consequence in measurement-summary.json: iss255.cases[3] = {evidencePairs:8, invalidCount:0, invalid:[], pass:true} -- i.e. ZERO wrong citations reported -- while run-results.jsonl line 10 accepts `spk:3 -> "Jubin"` on evidence turn 2026-08-24-uniaccess-leeds-arts-university-t088, and that turn's own speakerRef is spk:1 (checker re-derived: turn index 87, block 88, label spk:1, gold unnamed). Transcript text of t088 is spk:1 saying 'Hi. Hi. Hi. Hi, Jubin, go now.' -- an ADDRESS to a third party -- while t006 has spk:0 self-naming 'My name is Jubin Thakkar', so Jubin is spk:0, not spk:1 and not spk:3. All 8 accepted identities are of this same address/gratitude shape, which is exactly the failure class qa/gates/speaker-segment-identity.md was opened to catch.
fix_direction: The gate's bar-2 has three halves (label, name, citation); the citation half must be measured by an instrument INDEPENDENT of the acceptance rule, per D-015. Minimum: assert that each cited turn's own speakerRef equals the identity's speakerRef (self-naming), or -- for address/called-on evidence -- that the cited turn is adjacent to a block of that label AND that the gold/derived direction points at the claimed label rather than away from it (the ISS-255 handover-direction rule, applied to scoring rather than only to acceptance). Reporting invalidCount:0 from a predicate the acceptor already satisfied is not a measurement. This defect SURVIVES the ISS-282 fix: if a future cycle raises identity precision, this half of bar 2 would still certify wrong citations as valid.

title: scripts/webinar/sync-session.mjs deletes a session's turns and graph_edges then re-inserts them one-by-one with no transaction and no rollback on partial failure
evidence: scripts/webinar/sync-session.mjs:169-181 (unchanged logic from scripts/sync-webinar-session.mjs, only moved+re-pathed in cycle 1): `const del = await turnsColl(tenantId).deleteMany({ sessionId }); for (const t of turns) await turnsColl(tenantId).insertOne(strip(t));` and `const delE = await graphEdges(tenantId).deleteMany({ sessionRef: sessionId }); for (const e of edgeList) await graphEdges(tenantId).insertOne(e);` -- both delete-then-loop-insert with no session/transaction wrapper and no try/catch around the loop itself (the outer try/finally only closes the Mongo connection on error, it does not restore or roll back). If insertOne throws partway (network blip, validation error, process kill), the session is left with its OLD turns/edges already deleted and only a PARTIAL new set inserted -- a silent partial-write, not a caught failure the operator sees as 'still has old data'. This directly undermines contract meeting-bot-live-capture.md C8 (every graph_edges row's evidence[].turnId must resolve to a turns row of the same session) and C7's re-run-replaces-cleanly guarantee: a failed mid-run leaves exactly the inconsistent state C7/C8 exist to prevent.
fix_direction: Wrap each collection's delete+re-insert pair in a Mongo session/transaction (packages/db already has a client; use client.startSession()+withTransaction()), or at minimum build the new turns/edgeList arrays fully in memory (already done) and use insertMany inside a try/catch that on failure leaves the OLD rows in place (delete AFTER a successful insertMany of the new set, not before) rather than delete-then-loop-insert. Filed per checker dispatch instruction on the webinar-bot-live cycle-1 check (2026-09-24) after independently reading the current file; this is a pre-existing gap in logic the maker moved but did not change this cycle, so it is not counted against ISS-285/286/287's fix quality.
